title: Piclizer for Business
intro: Piclizer is a set of free online tools that run entirely in the web browser. Files are processed on the device that opens them — nothing is uploaded to a server and nothing is stored. No installs, no accounts, no licenses: that is what makes it a practical choice for teams that handle photos, documents and text every day.

ps: Most everyday file work — compressing a photo, merging two PDFs, cleaning a text export — is small, one-off, and not worth installing dedicated software for. Piclizer covers that work with a catalogue of free tools that open in a browser tab and work on the first try.

Because everything runs locally, the same site works in an office, in a school lab, or on a phone at a client site: the files never leave the device, so there is no upload step, no queue, and no server to breach.
bullets: No installs or updates — every tool works from a URL in any current desktop or mobile browser.
No accounts or logins — anyone on your team can use any tool immediately.
Local processing — images, PDFs, text and numbers are handled on the device and are never uploaded.
Free for everyone — no paywall, no license key, no per-seat cost.
Batch image work — compress, resize, crop, convert and watermark images; iPhone HEIC photos are supported end to end.
Combine up to 30 images into a single PDF, or merge up to 20 PDF files into one.
Bulk file tasks — rename many files in one pass and find duplicate files by their content.
Document preparation — page numbers, headers and footers, watermarks, rotation, page extraction and compression.
Text at scale — clean, deduplicate, sort, diff and convert text, JSON, CSV, XML, YAML and Markdown.
OCR for scanned documents — extract English or Arabic text from images and PDFs, with recognition running in the browser.
Marketing and e-commerce — resize and compress product photos, meet upload size limits exactly, prepare favicons and social banners.
Support and back office — merge and number PDFs, and clean or edit document metadata before sharing.
Education and exams — assemble PDFs from answer sheets and extract text from scanned papers.
Development — format JSON, XML, SQL and YAML, test regular expressions and decode tokens from the same browser tab as the code.

ps: Piclizer is a public website, not a platform. To keep expectations honest, here is what does not exist today:
bullets: No API or integrations — the tools are web pages, not a service you can call programmatically.
No accounts, dashboards or file storage — nothing is kept between visits, and no file is ever stored by us.
No self-hosting or enterprise licensing — the same free site is available to everyone.

ctaText: If you are evaluating Piclizer for your organisation and have a specific question — a requirement the current tools do not cover, a large-volume workflow, or anything else — send it through the contact form. Every message is read and answered by email; you can also reach us directly at piclizer@gmail.com.

faqs.q: Do our files go to your servers?
faqs.a: No. Image, PDF, text, calculator and developer tools process everything locally in the browser. Two tools make narrow, disclosed network requests: the OCR tools download the open-source Tesseract engine and its language data from a public CDN on first use, and the currency converter fetches a public exchange-rate table. In neither case are your files or inputs sent anywhere.

faqs.q: Does using Piclizer for business cost anything?
faqs.a: No. The same free tools are available to everyone — businesses included. There is no paid tier, no trial and no account requirement. (Where ads are displayed, they are only loaded after you accept advertising cookies.)

faqs.q: Can we use Piclizer on work devices without installing anything?
faqs.a: Yes. Every tool works from a URL in any current browser — desktop or mobile. There is nothing to install, update, patch or license, so it is easy to roll out across a team.

faqs.q: Is there an API we can integrate with?
faqs.a: Not today. Piclizer tools are browser pages rather than a programmable API. If a programmatic interface would help your workflow, tell us about it through the contact form — that kind of feedback is the main input for what gets built next.
